extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, administrative law practitioners, and members of the public who participate in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements under 5 U.S.C. § 553 (the APA notice-and-comment rulemaking provision) governing when and how agencies must provide notice, opportunity to comment, timing for effectiveness, and related exceptions. Intended to guide agency rule drafting, publication, and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applicability and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies, according to the provisions thereof, except to the extent that there is involved— (1) a military or foreign affairs function of the United States; or (2) a matter relating to agency management or personnel or to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories of matters to which §553 does not apply; agencies should assess whether proposed action falls into these excluded categories before applying §553 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General notice publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register, unless persons subject thereto are named and either personally served or otherwise have actual notice thereof in accordance with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default obligation is publication in the Federal Register; limited exception where affected persons are specifically named and personally served or otherwise have actual legal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirement — statement of time, place, and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rule making proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must describe logistical details of any public proceedings in the notice so interested persons know how to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirement — reference to legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include reference to the legal authority under which the rule is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the statutory or other legal basis for the proposed rule so commenters understand the agency's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirement — terms/substance or description of subjects/issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide either the full text (or substantive terms) of the proposal or a clear description of the issues so the public can give informed comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirement — regs.gov plain-language summary (≤100 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include the Internet address of a summary of not more than 100 words in length of the proposed rule, in plain language, that shall be posted on the Internet website under section 206(d) of the E‑Government Act of 2002 (commonly known as regulations.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must post a plain-language summary (max 100 words) at the specified website and include its URL in the Federal Register notice; this paragraph was added by Pub. L. 118–9 (2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to notice/hearing requirement (interpretative rules, policy statements, organizational/procedural rules; good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when notice or hearing is required by statute, this subsection does not apply— (A) to interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of agency organization, procedure, or practice; or (B) when the agency for good cause finds (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor in the rules issued) that notice and public procedure thereon are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categorical exemptions and the 'good cause' exception; agencies relying on good cause must publish and incorporate the finding and brief reasons in the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to participate (written submissions and oral presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice required by this section, the agency shall give interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making through submission of written data, views, or arguments with or without opportunity for oral presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide a meaningful opportunity for written comment and may allow oral presentations; procedures should enable submission of data, views, and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to state concise general statement of basis and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration of the relevant matter presented, the agency shall incorporate in the rules adopted a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules must include a concise general statement explaining the basis and purpose of the adopted rule, reflecting consideration of the comments and relevant materials submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative procedures where statute requires on-the-record hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When rules are required by statute to be made on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing, sections 556 and 557 of this title apply instead of this subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a statute mandates trial‑like on‑the‑record hearings, the formal adjudication procedures (5 U.S.C. §§556–557) govern rather than the informal notice-and-comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for effective date — 30‑day publication/service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The required publication or service of a substantive rule shall be made not less than 30 days before its effective date,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard waiting period giving the public time to adjust to new substantive rules; agency should set effective dates consistent with this minimum unless an exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the 30‑day effective date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions: (1) a substantive rule which grants or recognizes an exemption or relieves a restriction; (2) interpretative rules and statements of policy; or (3) as otherwise provided by the agency for good cause found and published with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists when the 30‑day delay is not required, including agency good cause (which must be found and published with the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition for issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall give an interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain procedures allowing interested parties to request rulemaking or changes to existing rules.
